reviewUnits.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.

reviewUnits.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。

translations.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.

reviewUnits.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」

translations.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter the crown prince: "Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?"

reviewUnits.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」

translations.literal: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, 'Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she saw him angry or pleased she would sigh, "Your Highness does not know how to wield awe and punishment—how will the realm ever fear and obey!"

reviewUnits.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。

translations.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.

reviewUnits.zh: 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲。

translations.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.

reviewUnits.zh: 愛埤車小馬，令左右馳騎，斷其鞅勒，使墮地為樂。

translations.literal: He loved low carts and ponies, ordering attendants to gallop them, cutting cheek-straps and cheek-pieces so riders fell for sport.
translations.idiomatic: He staged pony-cart wrecks for amusement.

reviewUnits.zh: 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之。

translations.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.
translations.idiomatic: He thrashed servants himself.

reviewUnits.zh: 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋。

translations.literal: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.
translations.idiomatic: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.

reviewUnits.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。

translations.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ran a palace bazaar—himself butchering, selling ale, and weighing coin.

reviewUnits.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。

translations.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's trade drew him to the stall.

reviewUnits.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.
translations.idiomatic: He peddled greens, dye seed, chicken, and flour from West Garden for cash.

reviewUnits.zh: 東宮舊制，月請錢五十萬，備於眾用，太子恆探取二月，以供嬖寵。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.
translations.idiomatic: He drew double stipends to bankroll favorites.

reviewUnits.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。

translations.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.

reviewUnits.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。

translations.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi warned Yu to cultivate virtue—Jia was not his mother.

reviewUnits.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。

translations.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pinned needles into Du Xi's seat cushion.

reviewUnits.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。

translations.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.

reviewUnits.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。

translations.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.

reviewUnits.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。

translations.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
translations.idiomatic: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.

reviewUnits.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。

translations.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Prince Chengdu of Ying saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Prince Chengdu of Ying saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

reviewUnits.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。

translations.literal: And I secretly hear him say: After the empress dies I will butcher her like fish on the block.
translations.idiomatic: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.

reviewUnits.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。

translations.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He warned Yu would purge Jia kin like the Yang coup.

reviewUnits.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」

translations.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."

reviewUnits.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。

translations.literal: Heaven gives you ale so Daowen may recover.
translations.idiomatic: She tied drinking to son's health.

reviewUnits.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。

translations.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.

reviewUnits.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。

translations.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Empty stomach worried him.

reviewUnits.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。

translations.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.
translations.idiomatic: He feared drunken copying.

reviewUnits.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！

translations.literal: Chen Wu relayed again: What unfilial piety!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu called him unfilial.

reviewUnits.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？

translations.literal: Heaven gives you ale and you refuse—is there poison inside?
translations.idiomatic: She accused refusal of hiding guilt.

reviewUnits.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。

translations.literal: Then you may drink two sheng—leave one sheng to carry back to Eastern Palace and finish.
translations.idiomatic: They compromised at two sheng plus one to go.

reviewUnits.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。

translations.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.
translations.idiomatic: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.

reviewUnits.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。

translations.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.

reviewUnits.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。

translations.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.

reviewUnits.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。

translations.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Lü jailed and starved Yu; sympathizers smuggled food over walls.

reviewUnits.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.

reviewUnits.zh: 時年二十三。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-three.

reviewUnits.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。

translations.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

reviewUnits.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。

translations.literal: Privately I wished him branded body and bone to rethink filial duty and kneel repentance rectifying his title.
translations.idiomatic: She posed as hoping Yu could repent posthumously.

reviewUnits.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。

translations.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.
translations.idiomatic: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.

reviewUnits.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。

translations.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.
translations.idiomatic: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.

reviewUnits.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."

reviewUnits.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。

translations.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.
translations.idiomatic: Parallel to Jin Prince Shen Sheng.

reviewUnits.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。

translations.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Yu died east at Xu.

reviewUnits.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！

translations.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!
translations.idiomatic: Universal mourning asserted.

reviewUnits.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。

translations.literal: Huguan's steadfast lord—autumn-thousand years awakened self.
translations.idiomatic: Allusion to righteous remonstrance.

reviewUnits.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。

translations.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.
translations.idiomatic: Justice spans dynasties.

reviewUnits.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。

translations.literal: Imperial grandson begins enthronement—great fortune your sons.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Zang named heir.

reviewUnits.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。

translations.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Hope for surviving line.
